output.summary: KEP-2257 proposed a kubectl plugin framework (the Kui project: kui plugin, kui-core framework, and kui-template boilerplate) that adds graphical popups to normal kubectl CLI commands, distributed via krew. Its status is implementable at stage alpha.
output.rationale: The KEP addresses the split between CLI tools and browser-based consoles by offering graphical popups launched from the terminal. Goals include a kui plugin, a reusable kui-core API, a template repo, and krew installation with minimal perturbation of krew. The status is implementable (from 2021-01-28), and the sources give no reason for stage or later changes beyond the July 2021 comment that KUI moved to kubernetes-sigs.

alternatives.option: Thin plugin strategy with a chain loader (kui-loader) for krew installation
alternatives.why_not: The readme describes it only as an alternate approach that would require development of a chain loader; a prototype exists (kask), but the sources do not say it was chosen.

alternatives.option: Fat plugins, each bundling its own copy of kui-core and Electron
alternatives.why_not: The readme describes this as the default distribution scheme, which requires only symlink support in krew's tarball extraction; the sources do not say it was rejected, and it has drawbacks such as a separate Chromium copy per plugin window.

evidence.quote: This enhancement offers a kubectl plugin framework that allows kubectl and kubectl plugins the ability to have graphical popups in response to normal CLI commands.
The minimal krew integration should only depend upon support for symlinks in its tarball extraction logic.
An alternate krew integration story, which we refer to as the "thin plugin" strategy, would require development of a chain loader.
KUI was already migrated to https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kui and it's one of the official sig-cli sub-projects
